title: RBAC policy templates and compact editor brainstorm
body:
Purpose / quick summary:
This is a working brainstorm for a compact RBAC policy template editor that lives inside Org -> Teams -> Access. Goal: let admins quickly apply common role patterns (read-only for infra, embed-only keys, limited-deploy) without leaving the console, preview the effective permissions, and reduce helpdesk tickets from mis-scoped keys.

Design goals / constraints:
- Compact: fits inside the existing right-side panel (no full-page rewrite for initial ship).
- Discoverable templates (search + tags) and a lightweight custom editor for ad-hoc edits.
- Preview of effective permissions + impacted resources before apply.
- Versioned templates + apply-as-canary (apply to 5% of users/teams first).
- Audit-friendly: every template instantiation creates an audit entry with diff.
- Safe-by-default: templates should include recommended guardrails (e.g., no wildcard resources unless explicitly enabled).

Sketch notes (visuals to approximate wireframes):
- Panel layout (compact mode):
  - Header: Template name, last-updated badge, quick-help tooltip (1-line).
  - Left column (40%): Template library list with search box and tag chips (filters: source=redwood|org|custom). Each row shows: name, short blurb, risk level pill (low/medium/high). Hover shows quick preview.
  - Right column (60%): Editor + Preview tabs. By default show Preview.
  - Editor: two modes (Structured toggle / Raw JSON toggle). Structured shows high-level toggles: allow: [read, write, deploy, billing], resource scoping UI (dropdown + multi-select paths), expiry slider, apply-to (team/service-account). Raw JSON shows policy snippet in familiar policy schema (read-only until user clicks "Edit raw").
  - Footer: Apply button with dropdown (Apply now | Schedule | Apply canary 5%). Secondary: Save as custom template.

Preview details:
- Effective permissions matrix: rows = resources (projects, datasets, deployment-pools, keys), cols = actions (read, write, execute, manage). Green/amber/red icons.
- Impact estimate: list of potentially affected service accounts, routes, and any high-risk patterns (e.g., "wildcard buckets: 3 matches").
- Quick compliance note: if organization has a required guardrail (e.g., no external-network-bind), surface warnings with link to policy.

Template model ideas:
- Curated Redwood templates (managed by product/solutions): common combos like "Embed-only key", "Read-only infra", "Can deploy but not manage billing". Marked as managed and show a small lock icon (can't edit source template, but can copy to custom).
- Org-shared templates: created by org admins and visible to everyone in the org.
- Personal/custom templates: saved by users under their org. Version history available.

Editor details / compact interactions:
- Quick-suggest: start typing resource path "projects/" and show autofill of existing resources (pulled via API).
- Constraint builder: when toggling "write" show a small inline prompt "limit write to specific tags or pools?" with quick chips.
- Inline validation: show errors/warnings while editing (e.g., conflicting rules, missing principals).
- Keyboard-first: cmd-K to open template library, enter to apply. We should add small microcopy for these shortcuts.

Guardrails and safety flows:
- Block wildcards at first. Offer an override modal that requires a justification and tags the audit.
- Require a review step for high-risk templates (e.g., granting billing or org-level manage). Bridge to an approval flow (link to Confluence/PR process) — MVP: create task in org's approval queue.

Audit integration:
- When a template is applied, record: template-id, who applied, diff (old vs new), canary % and results (if canary).
- Audit viewer: clicking the audit icon in the editor opens the audit log pre-filtered to changes on the affected teams/resources. Show a small diff inline.

Migration / backward compatibility:
- Provide a ‘translate existing role’ helper that scans an existing custom role (legacy key policies) and creates draft template. This reduces friction when moving orgs to templates.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Template language: stick with JSON policy schema vs a simplified declarative UI model. Tradeoff: JSON gives parity with infra; structured UX is friendlier. Suggest MVP: structured + optional raw JSON.
- Canary behavior: should canary apply be supported across multiple teams simultaneously? MVP: limit to "apply to subset of members in a single team".
- Source of truth for resources: will the editor call the same resources API as the Console? Need SRE/infra input.
- Approvals: do we build a simple in-console approval queue (fast) or integrate with an existing ticketing system? Integration first-party is heavier but more durable.

Backlog / rough tasks (MVP scope, 2-week sprint estimates):
- Frontend: compact panel + template library UI (6d) - owner: @eli - JIRA:RBAC-312
- Frontend: structured editor + raw toggle + validation (5d) - owner: @maya - JIRA:RBAC-315
- Backend: template service + CRUD + versioning (6d) - owner: infra - JIRA:RBAC-329
- Backend: preview engine (simulate effective permissions) (5d) - owner: applied-ml (it's partly heuristics) - JIRA:RBAC-334
- Audit: structured diffs + canary tracking (3d) - owner: security - JIRA:RBAC-338
- Docs: help text + microcopy + admin guide (2d) - owner: docs - Linear: RB-921

Edge cases / adoption notes:
- Org size: for very large orgs we need paging in the resource autofill (don't load 100k entries). Consider fuzzy search + rate limit.
- Template sprawl: expose usage metrics for templates (how often applied, last used) and trash/rename UX.
- Delegation: allow teams to maintain their local templates, but surface org-managed recommendations.

Microcopy examples (to steal in UI):
- Apply modal header: "Apply template: Embed-only key (read-only embedding)"
- Preview banner: "This template grants read access to model embeddings; it cannot create new keys unless you select 'allow key creation'."
- Warning when saving wildcard: "Wildcard resource detected — this may affect N resources. Add a justification to save."

Next steps / meeting asks:
- Design: quick mockups for compact panel + a11y review -> show at weekly product sync (Tue).
- Infra: confirm resources API and expected rate limits.
- Security: define what qualifies as 'high-risk' and brief approval flow requirements.
- PM: prioritize whether canary is MVP or post-MVP.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep initial surface small; focus on read/write/deploy triage templates first.
- Reuse existing permission icons and matrix components from Activity view to speed dev.
- Follow-up: prototype keyboard-first flow (cmd-K -> search templates -> preview -> apply).

Related links / refs (local):
- existing access audit notes: access-management-audit-log-and-keys-ux-notes (see drive)
- role templates draft: role-templates-service-account-creation-flow-notes (see drive)
- PR for console list component: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/278

-- end of brainstorm --

(Informal doc: lots of TODOs and open Qs. This is intentionally concise; will expand into a formal PRD once we confirm infra constraints.)
